description:
Current revision (user approved: "better implement this"): initial defaults are defined by provider clauses in the existing Zaq.ConnectorConfig.Settings.defaults/1, not application configuration. Remove the config block and configuration injection from pure settings helpers. Saved values still win; selective preservation and runtime fallback remain. Replace obsolete custom-config fixture coverage with module-owned defaults coverage; retain override/idempotence/removal assertions. This supersedes any configuration-entry requirements below. No new module, migration, adapter callback or MFA.

Final ownership design (supersedes dedicated WhatsAppSettings and migration plans):
User requested a shared defaults mechanism and runtime fallback, approved implementation, and explicitly requested no new Beadwork issue. Existing epic reused.

ZAQ defines provider defaults directly in Zaq.ConnectorConfig.Settings.defaults/1; there is no channel_settings_defaults application config block. WhatsApp entry includes jido_chat.room_reply_policy=mention_required and ingress sync_history=false/sync_full_history=false. Zaq.ConnectorConfig.Settings provides provider defaults clauses, nested merge, preservation of saved keys covered by the defaults template, and effective runtime projections. Explicit supplied values win; unrelated settings retain historical replacement semantics. No provider-specific settings module is required for new adapters.

Engine ChannelConfig.create applies configured defaults before insert; existing confirmed linking and upsert creation share it. Generic changeset preserves configured default keys and validates shared reply policy. Transport validation remains in each adapter; WhatsApp rejects explicit nonboolean history flags during preparation. No new callback or MFA. The generic bridge forwards effective ingress settings on saved and authenticated paths; existing listener fingerprint handles restart, while reply-policy changes refresh handlers.

Legacy missing keys are resolved at runtime without writing DB rows. Both unshipped backfill migrations and their tests were removed. No migration is required for this epic. Changes to code defaults affect legacy keys still absent; explicit saved choices take precedence. No production/dev backfill was run in this session.

Adapter preserves configurable history options, authenticated profile/storage boundaries and strict RAM provider infrastructure. Core is unchanged. Minimal registry, single sink_mfa, authorization and existing reply admission/history separation remain.

Completed acceptance: module-owned defaults with empty fallback for other providers; new records persist defaults; explicit values and unrelated settings preserved on creation; saved default options survive partial updates; legacy runtime fallback makes no DB writes; adapter validation remains; no migrations/module; policy-only refresh and listener restart regressions pass. New tests replace the user-rejected dedicated validation/backfill tests. Existing unrelated tests unchanged. Final ZAQ mix q and 414 tests + 12 properties pass. Sibling last source validation 200 tests + 12 properties and mix q pass; no sibling source change in simplification.

Action reuse: extend existing Settings, ChannelConfig creation, confirmed linking and generic bridge projection. Pure configuration helpers introduce no Action/tool/route. No UI changes/E2E required. Delivery still tracked in .6: review approval, coverage/final precommit per workflow, authorized adapter publication and real dependency pin. Current local integration uses modified ignored adapter source matching sibling, not a published new lock SHA. No commit/push performed.

Sequence retained: .1 adapter -> .2 shared defaults/persistence -> .3 legacy runtime fallback -> .4 generic bridge lifecycle -> .5 regression/docs -> .6 review/delivery.

Required policies: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md;
docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md;
docs/services/channels.md. Read sibling AGENTS.md before sibling changes, Engine
guide before persistence work, and documentation hygiene before updating docs.
Read system-config guidance if touching encrypted fields (which should be avoided).
Preserve existing assertions. Obtain explicit approval before changing existing test
behavior; add focused tests first. No UI feature/E2E work is required by this refactor.
Commit, push, publishing dependency revisions, and merge require separate authorization.

comments.text: Implementation authorized by user: start implementing the epic. Baseline ZAQ f8832ada74bc13bdc27c53e9838fc490aeba11a3 and WhatsApp a0555694ffaabc589c89bec6b7c93fbba7f6ff5f are clean. Context: Engine ChannelConfig.changeset is shared by BO persistence/upsert and LinkedDeviceConfirmation through existing ConfirmLinkedDevice Action; Settings is pure projection; bridge handler closures capture runtime connector config. Runtime refresh fingerprint currently omits reply policy and must include it to rebuild handlers without listener restart. Package provider_child_specs controls Mnesia runtime; raw listener API retains explicit transport flags. Keep both saved-binding and trusted authentication preparation paths. Rollback criteria: unexpected changes to history/mention behavior, loss of nested settings/credentials, schema bypass of canonical confirmation, or tests requiring weaker assertions. Existing shared-adapter test fixture will move its same mention_required value from provider registry to connector settings, preserving its scenario/assertions. No other existing test behavior changes authorized. Scope excludes deferred zaq-v0p, UI features, core callbacks, Actions/tools or new MFAs.

User requested adjustment of the existing epic because the fixed-false implementation was wrong. Replaced authoritative scope and reopened children .1-.5; retained .6 open and existing dependency chain. Approved direction follows WidgetSettings.defaults -> Engine creation persistence -> ChannelConfig validation/DB -> generic ingress -> configurable WhatsApp adapter. Existing reply-policy/RAM work retained. Historical fixed-false requirements and completion claims are superseded. Planning only this turn; no source/test/docs/lock edits, commit or publication performed.

Reimplementation started on user instruction start implementing. Current source matches prior uncommitted epic work. Module-context: Engine owns persisted connector settings; adapter owns conversion of trusted binding plus allowlisted ingress to transport config; generic bridge forwards settings and owns listener lifecycle. State lifetimes: DB per connector, prepared config per startup, listener supervised by host. Invariants: sole sink, authenticated profile/storage, RAM provider policy, history capture/reply admission separation, other providers unchanged. Safe-refactor: change only history-option preparation, pure WhatsApp settings/default application through existing Engine paths, lossless local backfill, generic lifecycle comparison if needed. Roll back if trusted identity/storage can be overridden or explicit flags/settings are lost. User explicitly rejected fixed-false behavior and approved the revised epic/tests; revise only corresponding fixed-false assertions, preserve independent security assertions. No UI/E2E or new Action/tool/callback required.

User approved simplification: shared channel_settings_defaults configuration plus generic Settings merge at creation/runtime; remove dedicated WhatsAppSettings and both unshipped backfills, no new Beadwork issue. This supersedes dedicated-module and migration requirements in prior steps. Existing epic reused. User approval includes replacing tests of provider-specific persistence validation/backfills with shared-default/runtime-fallback tests; adapter retains boolean validation. Generic nested settings edits now merge saved maps, while explicit scalar/list/null values replace. Preserve reply-policy validation and authorization/storage boundaries; no new MFA or adapter callback. Changes limited to existing ZAQ work and existing test/docs owners.

Applied user-approved shared defaults simplification without creating an issue. Dedicated WhatsAppSettings and two migrations removed. Generic selective preservation keeps configured startup choices, not all historical unrelated keys; this avoids changing widget/email replacement semantics. Final checks pass: mix q; 414 tests + 12 properties; both diff checks. Runtime fallback verified without DB changes. No commits/push or dependency publication performed.

Implemented approved module-owned defaults revision. Settings.defaults/1 defines WhatsApp initial values and empty fallback (atom/string providers); removed channel_settings_defaults config and unused config injection from defaults/preserve/effective. Engine creation and changeset call the same helpers. Updated tests/docs. Action reuse: extend existing pure Settings defaults lookup; reuse ChannelConfig.create/changeset and confirmation flow; no new Action/tool or execution boundary. Obsolete custom-config fixture replaced with actual provider defaults; override, partial-edit removal, property idempotence and non-WhatsApp behavior retained. Validation: mix q passed; 415 tests + 12 properties, 0 failures; git diff --check passed. Logs /tmp/zaq-ho7-module-defaults-quality.log and /tmp/zaq-ho7-module-defaults-tests.log. No sibling edits, migration, commit or push. Existing review/publication/final validation gate remains in .6.

User requested consolidation of three newly added test files into existing suites. Moved persistence/changeset cases and property to channel_config_test; pure defaults/runtime projection cases and property to connector_config/settings_test; confirmation/replay cases to linked_device_confirmation_test; real Telegram policy/runtime cases to jido_chat_bridge_test. Removed the three new files. Assertions retained. Existing bridge global stub setup bypassed only for the moved tagged describe, preserving its original router path after an initial validation exposed inherited pipeline-stub interference. Action reuse: not applicable, test organization only; production unchanged. Final validation pending.

Consolidation validated: final mix q passed; same 415 tests and 12 properties, zero failures. git diff --check passed. Three new ZAQ test files removed with scenarios retained in four existing suites. Logs /tmp/zaq-ho7-consolidation-final-quality.log and /tmp/zaq-ho7-consolidation-final-tests.log. No production changes in this iteration, commit or push.
